To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphorylation of p65 at ser536 contributes to acquired resistance to cisplantin in HNSCC and that IKKβ inhibitor, CmpdA, sensitizes cisplatin resistant cells by blocking p65 ser536 phosphorylation.

IKK phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit p65 at ser536 contributes to cisplatin resistance, and that inhibition of the IKK/NFB signaling pathway by CmpdA sensitizes cisplatin resistant cells to chemotherapy.

NF-κβ is activated by phosphorylation at serine 36 by IKKs in HNSCC and targeting this pathway with a novel IKKβ-specific inhibitor may provide an effective therapeutic strategy to treat cisplatin-resistant head and neck squamaous cell carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of acquired cisplatin resistant in HNSCC and how to overcome this resistance.
the role of the IKK/NFKB pathway in acquired cisplatin resistant head and neck cancer and the potential therapeutic implications of this pathway in overcoming acquired cisplatin-resistance.
the role of NF-κβ in acquired cisplatin-resistant HNSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phosphorylation of p65 at Ser536 by IKKα and/or IKKβ plays a critical role in acquired cisplatin resistant in HNSCC cells.

the IKK/NFKB signaling pathway is an important mechanism in the acquired resistance of HNSCC cells to cisplatinum and that targeting the signaling pathway may provide therapeutic benefit in the treatment of advanced HNSCC.

our data suggest that NF-κΒ is an essential mediator of acquired cisplatin-resistance in HNSCC and that targeting NF-κΒ may provide a possible treatment option to overcome acquired cisplatin-resistant in HNSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IKKβ is the key kinase that phosphorylates NF-κB on serine 536 in HNSCC cells.
we found the NF-κB pathway was constitutively active in cisplatin-resistant HNSCC cell models.
IKK/Nf-κB plays an important role in acquired cisplatin-resistant in HNSCC and the IKK/NfκB signaling pathway is a possible target to overcome acquired cisplatin-resistance in HNSCC patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

IKKβ and IKKα are the key upstream kinases for phosphorylation of NF-kB at serine536, and IKKβ is a more important target for the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of cisplatin resistant head and neck squamus cell carcinoma.

IKK/NFKB signaling pathway may serve as an important mechanism in acquired cisplatin resistant in HNSCC and that IKKβ inhibitors may be a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome acquired cisplatin in head and neck cancer.

IKK/NFKB plays a critical role in cisplatin acquired resistance in HNSC and that targeting IKK/NFK-B signaling pathway may provide novel therapeutic methods to overcome cisplatin acquired resistant in HNSCC patients.
